pairs.subject: frame-direction
pairs.evidence: lib/frames/frames.ts:438 The frame model keys its picture by rhetorical beat kind (hook/turn/movement…) through a lookup table instead of a closed visual-function vocabulary, and it has no motif threads and no boundary declarations, so the arc-level obligations exist only as prompt prose that the validator cannot check.

techniques.evidence: lib/frames/sceneSpec.ts:271 reviewSceneSpecs collects refusals per beat, keeps applied, rejected and missing disjoint, fails the whole pass only on unusable JSON, and rethrows non-gate exceptions. Not realized: no single finding when most beats fail for the same reason, and the duplicate guard (line 264) fixes the unit at one scene per beat.

lib/frames/sceneSpec.ts:179 Plate, elements and texts are separate layers (frames.ts:3-11). ASKS_FOR_TEXT rejects glyph requests in the subject. A figure must cite a notebook fact, and a low-grade fact may not carry an exact figure.

lib/frames/sceneSpec.ts:148 Motion is required (12+ chars), may not move text, and is rejected when it restates the subject. FrameClip has no duration field by design (frames.ts:124), and no verb or easing whitelist is enforced (sceneSpec.ts:139-143).
lib/frames/shots.ts:204 The shot lane gives a reset beat exactly one shot. Weak evidence: the explainer gate allows one scene per beat and cannot count functions, because no function field exists.

lib/frames/frames.ts:438 There is no closed function vocabulary (evidence, comparison, mechanism, metaphor, reveal, state-change, texture with sub-roles). The seed subject (subjectFor, lines 525-538) is a template per rhetorical role, which is the slide-deck failure the standard names. A metaphor budget or image-led mode cannot be computed.

lib/frames/sceneSpec.ts:26 The SceneSpec has no named thread and no lifecycle op (establish, carry, change, reprise, retire). Motifs live only in the free-text rationale the prompt asks for, so the rule that change and reprise need an earlier establish is not machine-checked.

lib/frames/frames.ts:154 Frame carries plate, clip, elements, texts and rationale, but no carry/agent/refresh declaration for its join. Hold beats cannot say whether they keep the last picture or clear the screen.

pairs.registryProposal: per-beat-rejection says a rejected beat 'keeps the template output the pass exists to replace', and visual-function-vocabulary names a template keyed by rhetorical category as the slide-deck failure. Here the fallback seed is exactly that template (PROBLEM_OF by BeatKind). The standard could say whether the honest-fallback seed must itself be keyed by visual function, or whether a category-keyed seed is acceptable as long as it is marked unauthored, as this repo does by leaving `rationale` empty.

pairs.subject: frame-direction
pairs.evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/sceneSpec.ts:2 The landing cosmos is a procedural paper-collage parallax (sky, ridges, disc sheets, medallions) with no narration beats, no spoken lines and no cited figures. A case-insensitive search of app/_landing for beat, narration, factId, voiceover and visualFunction returned no hits, so the subject's precondition (deciding what is on screen while a beat is spoken) does not hold.
